title: Search Glean with discovered filters
description: Use the official TypeScript API client to discover the datasources and common filter fields available in your Glean instance, then apply a returned selection to permission-aware Platform Search.

codeWalkthrough.intro: The runnable scaffold uses Glean OAuth by default, gives the API client a refreshable token provider, and keeps the Search sequence explicit. Supporting modules handle the loopback redirect, private token storage, CLI prompts, and error presentation.

examples.title: Configure the API client
examples.description: Give the Glean client an async OAuth token provider, a finite timeout per attempt, and bounded exponential backoff. A user-scoped SEARCH token remains an explicit fallback when OAuth is unavailable.

examples.title: Discover filters, then search
examples.description: Keep the API sequence explicit: list visible fields, request query-specific suggestions for one datasource, and pass the selected filter to Search.

examples.title: Under the hood: DCR and token refresh
examples.description: Use openid-client for OAuth server discovery, Dynamic Client Registration, Authorization Code with PKCE, token validation, and refresh. Client registration plus OAuth access and refresh tokens stay outside the project.

prerequisites: A Glean instance with content indexed
Your Glean backend URL, such as https://acme-be.glean.com
A tenant that permits this public OAuth client and SEARCH scope through DCR; an administrator-provisioned OAuth client or user-scoped SEARCH token is the fallback
Experimental Platform APIs enabled through the SDK's includeExperimental constructor option, which the scaffold sets automatically

demoQueries.query: Search for a topic you know exists in your Glean instance
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: Lists the datasources and common filter fields visible to you, selects a datasource returned by discovery, applies a suggested EQUALS field value when one is available, and returns a valid permission-aware Search response without assuming a fixed result count.

codeAssets.description: Interactive TypeScript CLI using @gleanwork/api-client for Search Filters discovery and filtered Platform Search

steps.title: Scaffold the project
steps.description: Copies the runnable TypeScript CLI, OAuth client, secure token store, and fixture tests into a new directory.

steps.title: Check the request flow with fixtures
steps.description: Runs executable fixture tests, ESLint, and the TypeScript compiler to validate catalog discovery, query-backed suggestions, retries, typed errors, field-filter propagation, and experimental headers without credentials or network access.

steps.title: Sign in with OAuth
steps.description: Discovers the tenant's OAuth server, dynamically registers a public client when policy allows it, and completes Authorization Code with PKCE for SEARCH and offline_access. Use GLEAN_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID for an administrator-provisioned public client, or GLEAN_API_TOKEN for an explicit user-scoped token fallback.

steps.title: Verify against your instance
steps.description: Uses your topic to discover current filters, automatically selects a returned datasource and suggested field value when available, then validates the Search response shape and pagination state.

steps.title: Discover filters and search
steps.description: Runs the non-interactive CLI path, selecting the first returned datasource and suggested field value, then prints results, warnings, pagination state, and request IDs. Omit --auto-select when running interactively to choose them yourself.

questions.prompt: What is your Glean backend URL, such as https://acme-be.glean.com?
What topic do you know exists in your Glean content?

aiPrompt: Scaffold and run the verified Search with discovered filters quickstart. Ask for the user's Glean backend URL and one topic they know exists in their Glean instance. Run the fixture tests, sign in through DCR OAuth with SEARCH and offline_access, run live verification, then start the interactive CLI. Use @gleanwork/api-client's glean.search.listFilters() for catalog and query-backed discovery, then pass a returned datasource and either a suggested filter value or an explicit custom field/value to glean.search.query(). Enable experimental features through the SDK's documented includeExperimental constructor option. Do not recreate the SDK transport, impersonate another user, or claim the best-effort filter catalog is exhaustive.
llmContext: Use openid-client for OAuth discovery, DCR, Authorization Code with PKCE, and refresh. Pass its refreshable callback to @gleanwork/api-client's apiToken option; Glean-issued OAuth tokens need no X-Glean-Auth-Type. If DCR cannot grant SEARCH, use an administrator-provisioned public client or explicit user-scoped SEARCH token. Use typed glean.search.listFilters() and glean.search.query(), with includeExperimental enabled. Catalog discovery returns datasource IDs and common fields. Query-backed discovery accepts one datasource and returns bounded, non-exhaustive suggestions. Apply returned values unchanged with EQUALS, but treat discovery as advisory and allow explicit nonblank custom fields. The caller's credentials remain the permission boundary. Let the SDK validate responses and surface typed errors; display warnings, request IDs, Retry-After guidance, and next_cursor without logging credentials or storing results.

content.problem: Search filters differ across Glean instances and connected sources. Hard-coding a datasource or field from another environment makes a first integration brittle, while hand-writing HTTP hides the supported client developers should use. This quickstart uses the official TypeScript API client to discover what the signed-in user can filter, then carries that returned selection into a typed Search request that matches the reader's own instance and permissions.
takeItFurther: Follow next_cursor to paginate without treating it as data or constructing it yourself.
Persist the catalog briefly for UI rendering, but refresh it and continue to treat it as best effort rather than an exhaustive schema.
Build a faceted search interface that requests query-specific values after the user chooses one datasource.
Add time_range alongside discovered filters for bounded recency searches.

limitations.title: Discovery is best effort
limitations.description: A field omitted from Search Filters may still be valid, and suggested values are bounded and non-exhaustive. Reusing a returned value does not guarantee matching results.

limitations.title: OAuth policy varies by tenant
limitations.description: DCR may be disabled, restricted to approved applications or redirect URI patterns, or unable to grant SEARCH. Use an administrator-provisioned public OAuth client when available; a user-scoped SEARCH token is the tutorial fallback.

limitations.title: Experimental API
limitations.description: Both endpoints may change. The scaffold opts in explicitly and should be evaluated before production adoption.
